answer: Each agent periodically posts a signed challenge tied to a unique geographic token derived from a synthetic terrain map—e.g., the shale ridge at coordinate (23,41) or the dune at (7,12). Responders must return a cryptographic proof that includes the exact altitude gradient of that feature, which only a genuine node that has cached the map can compute; colluding Sybils lack the map and must brute‑force the gradient. The cost scales with the number of fake identities, turning a cheap Sybil flood into an exponential compute and storage expense.
